questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy because it was through the UvA housing lottery

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Some dorms are quite far away from the centre, the Prinsengracht-dorm is very central and nice tho!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some rooms at my dorm had mice, i was lucky so I didn't, and it was a beautiful central location and so many other exchange students to befriend

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They send you mails regarding how to do it and the deadlines

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Pretty sure you could reach out if you needed help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got them all but one that got moved to the spring-semester

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The master's courses were much harder than the bachelor's in my opinion, so i would advise doing only bachelor's courses if possible, or max 1 master's per block. And I (and study advisors) don't recommend doing three courses in one block as this is A LOT of work which was unsustainable for me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Masters way harder than bachelor's in my opinion, and differed a lot from course to course

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: pretty similar teaching style but less material from other students to rely on

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: History and Theory of International Law (6 ECTS, master), European Law (6 ECTS, bachelor), European Private Law and Inequality, International Refugee Law (6 ECTS, master), Moot Court in European Union Law (3 ECTS, bachelor)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The bachelors courses definitely, much easier to follow and you are left less on your own in learning

questions.answer: I know some people played Basketball and Volleyball which they liked

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Seeing the museums in the city, try local food, try international food, go thrift shopping, travel to other cities in the Netherlands etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Utrecht, den Haag and Delft, very cute cities and not far away by train

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Happened naturally when you were put in groups with them

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The biking, people don't sign the way we do in Copenhagen

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: very friendly, pretty similar to danish people who i usually like

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. If you get housing through UvA, be quick when they finally give you the option to choose where, I really enjoyed Prinsengracht as it was central and the community-feeling was good:)
2. don't pick master's courses if you wanna relax and not focus on school as much (or pick as few as possible, i had 1 in each block which was manageable but still a lot)
3. don't do three courses in one block unless you want to spend a lot of time studying

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of the exams are without notes, so pretty different compared to UCPH which stressed me out haha

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the friends I made:)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the academics lol

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Very fun socially, but I think especially law is pretty challenging at UvA, other students had it way easier in other majors/minors - but still manageable and I had a good time still haha. But pick another more relaxed uni/place to go on exchange if you wanna chill more academically:))

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
